data.name: Echoes of the Fey Episode 0: The Immolation
data.detailed_description:
Imagine being the only survivor of an explosion that kills thousands of people. That is the fate of Sofya Rykov. And survival is just the beginning of her tale...

***
NOTE: This game uses 3D graphics and lighting. Please check Minimum Specifications before playing to ensure a good experience
***

Episode 0: The Immolation is a free, standalone chapter in the Echoes of the Fey adventure game/visual novel series. This installment will serve as an introduction to players new to the series and provide important backstory to players who enjoyed Echoes of the Fey Episode 1: The Fox's Trail, already released on Steam. Play as Sofya Rykov, before she became a private investigator and before she was cursed with unstable magic powers. An officer in the Imperial Army, Sofya is tasked with guarding Leshin prisoners at Onigrad, a city which will soon become famous for its fiery destruction.

  • 3d environments and dynamic camera angles via our new UE4 implementation
  • English voice acting (expression lines)
  • Over 1 hour of story with multiple choice branches
  • Soundtrack featuring new songs and remixes of Episode 1 tracks reflecting the dread of the Immolation of Onigrad
  • A free introduction to a series which will span multiple episodes
  • Achievements and trading cards


In the last days of the long war between Humans and Leshin, a tense stalemate has emerged. For years, Leshin have lain siege to the Humans over their use of Fey reactors, massive machines that draw electricity from the realm of magic. Both sides tire after almost thirty years of war, and perhaps peace is now in reach. But Leshin extremists, desperate for a victory to reclaim their power among the people, are about to stage a devastating attack that will change the world forever.

Echoes of the Fey is a series of detective stories set in the high fantasy world of Oraz. Episode 0: The Immolation takes place before the protagonist, Sofya Rykov, becomes a private investigator. She is an officer in the Imperial Human army who believes she has secured a safe position as a prison guard in the metropolitan city of Onigrad. One fateful night, one of the Leshin assigned to her begins to act strangely. And then a massive boom rings out from the Onigrad Fey reactor...

Episode 0 is an adventure game/visual novel with dialog trees and several choices for Sofya that will affect the way the story plays out. Sofya will also be able to walk around the prison and learn more about the world from her prisoners, though with an impending disaster about to hit the prison, she will have to balance how to use her time before staging her escape.

reviews.review:
Echoes of the Fey Episode 0: The Immolation is a short, story-focused fantasy adventure that serves as a prequel to the larger Echoes of the Fey narrative. Developed and published by Woodsy Studio, it favors dialogue, character development, exploration, and player decisions over combat or elaborate mechanical systems. Its compact length makes it feel closer to an interactive novella than a traditional role-playing game, but within that limited scope it manages to establish an intriguing world and give its central character a meaningful origin story.

The narrative follows Sofya Rykov during an earlier stage of her life, before she becomes the private investigator seen elsewhere in the series. She is serving as an officer in the Imperial Human Army and has been assigned to guard Leshin prisoners in Onigrad. The assignment initially appears manageable, but the situation gradually becomes more disturbing as one of the prisoners begins behaving strangely. The tension eventually leads toward the catastrophic Immolation of Onigrad, an event that dramatically changes Sofya's life and becomes an important piece of the wider story.

Much of the appeal comes from the setting. Humans and Leshin have been trapped in a destructive conflict lasting almost three decades, and both sides are approaching a point where continuing the war has become increasingly difficult. The existence of Fey reactors adds an unusual technological element to the fantasy backdrop. Humans use these enormous devices to extract energy from a magical realm, creating a world where industrial technology and supernatural forces are closely intertwined. With peace seemingly within reach but extremists threatening that possibility, the political situation gives the story a larger sense of consequence.

Gameplay primarily consists of moving through environments, interacting with characters, investigating the situation, and selecting dialogue responses. The prison functions as more than scenery because talking with its inhabitants reveals additional information about the war and the different perspectives surrounding it. Sofya's military position places her on one side of the conflict, while her conversations with Leshin prisoners expose her to people whose experiences challenge a simple good-versus-evil interpretation of the situation.

Player choice is particularly important to the experience. Conversations provide several opportunities to determine Sofya's responses, while limited time encourages the player to decide which interactions deserve attention. These decisions do not transform the game into an enormous branching RPG, but they make the journey more personal and provide an incentive for another playthrough. Different choices can reveal additional pieces of information or slightly change how events and relationships are experienced.

Presentation combines visual-novel storytelling with three-dimensional environments created in Unreal Engine 4. Dynamic camera angles give conversations and important scenes a more cinematic quality than static character portraits alone could provide. The production values are clearly those of a smaller independent project, and some animations, character models, and environmental details are relatively basic. Even so, the restrained visual design generally works because the game depends more heavily on atmosphere and writing than spectacle.

Sound also contributes to the mood. English voice acting is used selectively through expression lines rather than providing full spoken dialogue for every conversation. It is a practical compromise that gives the characters some vocal identity without pretending to be a completely voiced production. The soundtrack does considerable atmospheric work, supporting both the quieter investigative moments and the increasingly ominous events surrounding the impending disaster.

The game's biggest weakness is also an unavoidable consequence of its purpose as Episode 0: it is very short. Players expecting an extensive adventure, substantial puzzle solving, deep character progression, or action-heavy encounters will probably find the mechanics too limited. The story can establish interesting political, magical, and personal ideas without always having enough time to explore them fully. Some characters and concepts feel as though they are introductions to material intended to receive greater attention elsewhere in the series.

At the same time, the concise runtime works surprisingly well for the structure. There is little unnecessary padding, and the approaching catastrophe keeps the story moving. Replayability comes from experimenting with different conversations and choices, while achievements and other Steam features provide a few additional goals. As a free introductory experience, it asks for relatively little investment while providing enough world-building to determine whether the larger universe is appealing.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unsupported. Players primarily interested in experiencing it on Valve's handheld should keep this limitation in mind rather than assuming that the simple controls automatically guarantee full compatibility. Its design may appear ideal for portable play, but the official Deck classification does not currently provide that assurance.

Ultimately, Echoes of the Fey Episode 0: The Immolation works best as a concentrated piece of interactive fantasy fiction. The mechanics are simple and the production is modest, but the combination of political tension, magical technology, dialogue choices, and an approaching tragedy gives the adventure a distinct identity. Sofya is an interesting protagonist precisely because the player encounters her before the experiences that will define her later life, making the events in Onigrad feel like more than a detached historical incident.

For players interested in narrative adventures, visual novels, fantasy mysteries, and choice-driven storytelling, this is a worthwhile introduction to its fictional universe. Its short duration and mechanical simplicity prevent it from becoming a particularly substantial standalone adventure, but its atmosphere and world-building compensate for many of those limitations. As a focused prequel designed to provide context while telling its own tragic story, it accomplishes its purpose effectively.

Rating: 8/10
